title: Check yourself: loading and initialising classes

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A service runs `Exporter e; if (config.legacy()) { e = new LegacyExporter(); } else { e = new JsonExporter(); }`, where `Exporter` is an abstract class and `LegacyExporter`'s static block logs "legacy exporter ready". It starts with legacy off and `-Xlog:class+load`, and the log has a load line for `LegacyExporter`. Does "legacy exporter ready" appear in the log?

options.text: Yes, since the JVM runs a class's static block as part of loading the class
options.says: loading creates the Class object; the static block runs at initialisation, on the first new, static call or non-constant static field read

options.text: No, since the static block runs only when code first creates or otherwise uses the class
options.says: the verifier can load a class to check the assignment, but initialisation waits for a first use such as new, which never happens

options.text: Yes, since a load line shows that the branch naming the class has run
options.says: the verifier loads classes before main runs, so a load line doesn't mean the branch ran

options.text: No, since the load lines list the class path at start-up, before any class is used
options.says: classes are loaded when code or the verifier first needs them, not by scanning the class path at start-up

origin.section: A Class Is Loaded When Code First Needs It, and Initialised Only When Code First Uses It

questions.stem: A test runner creates `URLClassLoader child = new URLClassLoader(new URL[] {fixturesDir}, ClassLoader.getSystemClassLoader())`. The `fixturesDir` directory is also on the application's class path. What does `child.loadClass("OrderFixture").getClassLoader()` return?

options.text: The application loader, since the child asks its parent first and the parent finds OrderFixture on its class path
options.says: loadClass asks the parent first; the application loader finds OrderFixture on the class path and defines it

options.text: The child loader, since the loader that is asked for a class is the one that defines it and returns it
options.says: the loader asked can pass the request to its parent; getClassLoader() reports the loader that defined the class

options.text: The application loader, since the application loader defines every class on the class path, whichever loader is asked
options.says: a loader that defines before asking its parent (child-first) would define its own copy; here the class comes from the application loader because the child asks it first

options.text: The child loader, since a loader passes a request to its parent only for classes in java.* packages
options.says: parent-first applies to every name: the parent is asked first whatever the package

origin.section: Each Loader Asks Its Parent First, So the JDK's Classes Always Come from the JDK's Loaders

questions.stem: `class Limits { static final Plan FREE = Plan.FREE_PLAN; static final int MAX_SEATS = 5; static final int MAX_PROJECTS = Integer.getInteger("projects", 3); }` and `class Plan { static final Plan FREE_PLAN = new Plan(Limits.MAX_SEATS, Limits.MAX_PROJECTS); ... }`. No system property is set, and the first code to run reads `Limits.FREE`. What does that plan hold?

options.text: 5 seats and 3 projects, since the seat count is part of Plan's compiled code and the project count is computed when Plan first reads it
options.says: a field read during the same thread's initialisation of Limits returns its current value; MAX_PROJECTS is computed later, in textual order

options.text: 5 seats and 0 projects, since the seat count is part of Plan's compiled code and the project count is still unset when Plan reads it
options.says: MAX_SEATS is a compile-time constant that javac copies into Plan; MAX_PROJECTS is computed after FREE, so Plan reads its default

options.text: 0 seats and 0 projects, since the seat count and the project count are both still unset when Plan reads them
options.says: MAX_SEATS is a compile-time constant that javac copies into Plan, so it is 5 whatever state Limits is in

options.text: An ExceptionInInitializerError, since the seat count and the project count belong to a class whose initialisation has not finished
options.says: the same thread may read a class it is initialising; the read returns the current value without an error

origin.section: Static Initialisers Run in Textual Order, and a Cycle Lets Code Read a Field Before It Is Set

questions.stem: A service sometimes never finishes starting. Its monitoring agent calls `ThreadMXBean.findDeadlockedThreads()` every minute and reports nothing. The CPU is idle, and a stack trace of each thread shows `main` in `Inventory.<clinit>` and `scheduler` in `Catalog.<clinit>`, both in state RUNNABLE. What is going on?

options.text: Each thread waits for the other to finish initialising a class, and the agent misses it since the lock held during class initialisation is not one that check examines
options.says: a class initialisation cycle reached from both ends is a deadlock that findDeadlockedThreads doesn't report; a thread dump shows the class initialization monitor

options.text: Both threads are still working through their static initialisers, since a thread that waits for another thread shows as BLOCKED or WAITING
options.says: on Java 21 a thread waiting for another thread's class initialisation reports RUNNABLE

options.text: Each thread waits for the other to finish initialising a class, and the agent misses it since the check runs once a minute and the threads were not waiting when it ran
options.says: the hang lasts until the process is killed, so the threads are waiting every time the check runs; the check doesn't examine class initialisation at all

options.text: Both threads are still working through their static initialisers, since findDeadlockedThreads reports two threads that wait for each other
options.says: it covers monitors and ownable synchronizers only, not class initialisation

origin.section: Two Threads That Initialise a Cycle from Both Ends Wait for Each Other Forever

concepts: A compile-time constant is copied into the reading class by javac, so reading it neither initialises its class nor sees a default value.

Two threads that initialise a class cycle from both ends wait for each other forever; on Java 21 they report RUNNABLE, findDeadlockedThreads returns null, and a thread dump names the class initialization monitor.
A class is loaded when code or the verifier first needs it, and its static initialisers run only at its first use, such as new, a static method call or a non-constant static field read.
ClassLoader.loadClass returns a class it already loaded, else asks its parent, and defines the class itself only when the parent can't, so the loader asked is not always the loader that defines.
